svg.aria-label: The 3-2-1 backup rule and why only an offline or immutable copy survives a ransomware attack that reaches connected backups.
svg.title: Why backups are the real ransomware defence — and why the connected ones die
svg.text: THE 3-2-1 RULE — AND WHY RANSOMWARE ONLY SPARES ONE OF THEM
copies of your data —
the original + two backups.
different media / systems,
so one failure can't take both.
copy kept OFF-SITE and
OFFLINE or immutable.
THE ATTACKER REACHES EVERYTHING THAT IS CONNECTED
Online / connected backups
A network share, a mapped drive, a
backup server on the domain — the
attacker with domain admin encrypts
or deletes these too (vssadmin delete).
Offline / immutable copy
Air-gapped tape, or immutable cloud
object-lock that cannot be altered.
Unreachable from the network → it
SURVIVES. This is what restores you.
reachable = encrypted
TWO TRUTHS THAT SEPARATE SURVIVING FROM PAYING
A backup you've never restored isn't a backup
Untested backups fail silently — corrupt, incomplete,
or missing the one system that matters. Recovery is a
rehearsed drill, measured by RTO (how long to be back)
and RPO (how much data you can afford to lose).
Backups beat encryption — not double extortion
Good backups let you rebuild without paying for a
decryptor. But if the attacker also STOLE the data first,
restoring does not un-leak it — which is exactly why
modern crews exfiltrate before they encrypt.
